alerts.reason: June net sales grew only 3.2% despite price increases. Component shortages delayed shipments and contributed to a $21.5 million inventory build (A–C). I expect pricing to keep September sales growth above -5%, but continued difficulty completing shipments could push December sales at least 5% below the prior year.

Services growth of 6% offset a 3% Products decline, leaving total revenue up 3%. Restrictions in Suzhou had already reduced genomic services orders and production (A, B). I expect Services to keep September consolidated growth above -5%, with fewer orders feeding into December revenue and pushing growth to -5% or lower.

June sales volume fell, and weaker Mobile Solutions demand partly offset gains elsewhere. Customer pricing recovered some inflation, but ordering was uneven (A, C, E). I expect pricing to keep September reported sales growth above -5%, then further volume losses to push December growth to -5% or lower.

Blue Apron tied revenue growth and further advertising increases to $70 million of pending financing or alternative funds (A, B). The prior year's marketing increase began late in Q4 (D), making December a tougher comparison than September. I forecast September growth above -5% and a December decline of at least 5% if funding limits customer acquisition.

June net sales fell about 1%. Higher module volume partly offset a lower selling price per watt (A, D). I expect volume to keep September growth above -5%, but forecast a December decline of at least 5% if selling prices continue falling faster than unit sales grow.

June revenue rose $78.7 million as revenue per mile increased 14.4%, but revenue miles per tractor per week fell 6.7%. Softer volumes persisted through June, and the spot market had weakened sequentially since March (A, B, D). I expect rate gains to keep September growth above -5%, then fading rate support and lower utilization to push December revenue down at least 5% year over year.
